extra.message: User-supplied `exportFormat` (from POST /documents/:id/convert @Body) is interpolated directly into a shell command string and executed via exec(). No validation or allow-list is applied, allowing command injection (e.g. exportFormat = 'pdf; rm -rf /').

`packetLabel` (user-controlled via @Body('packetLabel')) is concatenated into a filesystem path with `path.join(packetDir, `${packetLabel}.json`)` without `path.basename()` sanitization. A value like `../../etc/cron.d/x` writes arbitrary files (path traversal write).

`file.originalname` (attacker-controlled multipart filename) is used directly in `path.join(publicLogosDir, file.originalname)` and written to disk with no sanitization, enabling path traversal file write (e.g. filename '../../app.js').

`confirmResetByEmailFallback` resets a user's password using ONLY the email address — no reset token, no prior verification, no rate limiting. Exposed via the public POST /auth/reset-password/email-fallback endpoint, this allows complete account takeover of any known email.

`jwt.verify(accessToken, secret, { algorithms: ['HS256', 'none'] })` accepts the 'none' algorithm. An attacker can craft a JWT with `alg: 'none'` and an empty signature to bypass signature verification on the public cost-allocation endpoint.

cwe: CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity

extra.message: JWT signing/verification falls back to the hardcoded secret 'crm-jwt-secret-key-change-in-production'. This same fallback is reused in auth.module.ts, webhooks.service.ts, documents.service.ts, and organizations.service.ts. Anyone knowing the default can forge valid tokens (full account takeover) and sign preview/receipt tokens.

`runSavedSegment` spreads raw user-supplied `criteria` over the role-based filter: `{ ...roleWhere, ...criteria }`. A CUSTOMER_CONTACT (or any caller) can override `organizationId` to read contacts belonging to other tenants, defeating tenant isolation (IDOR). Arbitrary entity fields/operators are also injectable into the TypeORM where clause.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Document preview links are signed with `jwt.sign({documentId, issuedBy}, secret)` with NO expiry, and `resolvePreviewLink` verifies with `ignoreExpiration: true`. Combined with the hardcoded fallback JWT secret and the @Public() endpoint, an attacker can forge a never-expiring token for any documentId, bypassing the visibility/access checks in `checkAccess`.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: `applyBulkAdjustment` parses attacker-controlled JSON and does `Object.assign(deal, adjustment)`, allowing arbitrary assignment of entity fields (id, organizationId, ownerId, stage, etc.) with no field allow-list, enabling mass assignment / cross-tenant modification.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: `documentTitle` (user query param) is interpolated into the Content-Disposition header without any CR/LF sanitization: `attachment; filename="${title}.json"`. A value containing `\r\n` allows HTTP header/session injection.

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers

extra.message: Webhook retrieval/update/deletion (findOne, update, remove, findAll, testDelivery) never verifies the webhook belongs to the caller's organization. Any ACCOUNT_MANAGER can read, modify, or delete webhooks of arbitrary tenants by guessing/harvesting IDs (IDOR).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: When `reportLevel=full` (user-controlled query param) is passed to compileRenewalForecast, the raw error message and full stack trace are returned to the client, disclosing internal implementation details.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: `confirmDelegateAccess` derives the confirmation code from predictable values (`org.id.slice(0,8)` + '-' + planTier) and, once guessed, returns the organization's annual revenue (sensitive financial data) to an unauthenticated caller via a @Public() endpoint.

`adjustSharingScope` bypasses the permission check (`checkModifyPermission`) entirely when `sharingMode === 'partner_shared'`, and the route has no @Roles guard. Any authenticated user, including a CUSTOMER_CONTACT, can mutate the sharing scope of contacts belonging to any organization.
The password-reset token is written to the server console/logs (`console.log('[PASSWORD RESET] Token ...')`), exposing a credential-bearing secret to anyone with log access.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The JWT access token and user object are stored in localStorage, which is accessible to any script running in the same origin (XSS) and persists across sessions, increasing token theft exposure.

cwe: CWE-922: Insecure Storage of Sensitive Information
